source.title: Faithful Heteroscedastic Regression with Neural Networks
source.venue: Proceedings of the 26th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), PMLR vol. 206

confidence_rationale: Directly on-point and high-fidelity for SD-063's central validity risk. It rigorously documents that the standard Gaussian-NLL heteroscedastic head corrupts the mean estimate (rich-get-richer via 1/sigma^2 gradient scaling), which (a) explains why hetero_gaussian lost to quantile_pinball in V3-EXQ-712 -- supporting SD-063's form choice -- but (b) warns that ANY conditional-uncertainty head coupled to the mean/encoder during joint training can degrade the point prediction, which is exactly SD-063's open, unresolved concern. Mixed because it both corroborates the form decision and raises a concrete failure mode for the wired-in build.
failure_signatures: Minimising a heteroscedastic Gaussian NLL scales the mean gradient by 1/sigma^2(x), biasing learning toward low-variance points and creating a 'rich-get-richer' cycle where poorly-predicted points get high variance to explain away poor mean estimates rather than improving them; the resulting mean can be significantly less accurate than an equally-expressive mean-only (MSE) model.

The pathology arises specifically when mean and variance share ancestral computations (a shared trunk) and are optimised jointly -- the exact configuration a wired-in E2 uncertainty head would create -- so SD-063's joint-training validation gate is precisely where this failure would manifest.

Beta-NLL (Seitzer 2022) and the paper's stop-gradient fix are needed to recover faithful means; a naive joint head does not, meaning SD-063's head must be explicitly shielded or the E2 mean/agency-residual (SD-031) could be corrupted.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Neural heteroscedastic regression trained by Gaussian-NLL minimisation produces mean estimates that are provably and empirically less accurate than an equally-expressive mean-only model, because the 1/sigma^2(x) gradient weighting biases the mean toward low-noise regions; a stop-gradient / Newton-step modification restores a 'faithful' mean equal to the mean-only baseline while retaining best-in-class variance calibration.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-063 rejected the hetero_gaussian E2 head in favour of a distribution-free quantile/pinball head, and requires that a wired-in conditional-uncertainty head (a) preserve the CRPS / precision-error-corr advantage under JOINT training and (b) not explain away the SD-031 E2WorldForward agency residual. Stirn et al. give the mechanistic reason the Gaussian form is dangerous (mean corruption via variance-weighted gradients) -- corroborating the form choice -- and simultaneously show that the corruption is a general joint-training hazard for conditional-variance heads sharing a trunk, which is exactly SD-063's open risk.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The analysis is specific to the Gaussian-NLL parameterisation; the quantile/pinball head SD-063 uses does not have the 1/sigma^2 gradient term, so it is NOT automatically subject to the same rich-get-richer pathology -- the paper is a warning-by-analogy, not a direct measurement of a pinball head's joint-training behaviour. Whether a pinball head coupled to E2's encoder corrupts the mean or absorbs the SD-031 agency residual is an empirical question SD-063's own validation experiment must answer.
mapping.source_context: Regression benchmarks (UCI datasets, a CRISPR-guide-efficacy genomics application, and image regression); parametric Gaussian heteroscedastic networks with shared and separate mean/variance heads.

confidence_components.notes: Strong peer-reviewed AISTATS analysis with theorem + broad empirics. High mapping fidelity: it speaks directly to SD-063's two open validation conditions (joint-training survival and not-explaining-away a residual). Transfer risk moderate because the sharpest result is Gaussian-specific and SD-063's head is quantile-based; the hazard transfers as a caveat, not as a proven defect of the chosen form.
